newsitem.title: INDIA: India "pragmatic" on external commercial borrowing.
newsitem.headline: India "pragmatic" on external commercial borrowing.

text.p: Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia said on Thursday that the Indian government would be "pragmatic" in approving more external commercial borrowing by private firms, but within an overall cap.

"Government will be quite willing to be pragmatic about doing more external borrowings but with the cap very much in mind," Ahluwalia said in response to a question by a businessman at a seminar in the Indian capital.
The businessman had suggested that the government should be more liberal in approving companies' demands to borrow overseas.

"I'm quite hopeful in the coming year if the inflation looks reasonably under control, we will be able to see a much higher inflow of funds," Ahluwalia said, explaining the government's intentions to let private firms' overseas borrowings rise.
He said that two years ago, the government had set an informal cap of $5 billion per year in aggregate external commercial borrowings, and in the past year had raised it to $7 billion.
Ahluwalia is the highest ranking civil servant in the Finance Ministry.
